summary: padding-driven batcher holdback for short requests causing p99 latency spikes
description:
Issue summary: BrightChat reported sudden p95/p99 latency regressions and intermittent 504s during a marketing-driven burst. The increase was concentrated on short-request traffic (<= 32 tokens). Impact: Customer-facing chat UI experienced delayed first-token times and several user timeouts, causing user-visible errors and an increase in support tickets. Environment: prod / us-east (dedicated cluster), serving runtime v2.13.1, batcher v1.8.0. Observed window: 2026-03-11 16:10 - 17:05 UTC.

Expected behavior: Short, single-turn inference requests should be batched quickly and served under SLO; p99 should not spike above slotted SLOs during short bursts.

Actual behavior: p95 remained acceptable but p99 increased to ~1.2s (baseline ~180ms) for short requests; a tail subset experienced >3s and occasional 504s. Spikes correlate with mixed traffic—short requests interleaved with long-sequence generation from same tenant.

Notes: This ticket focuses on batch formation behavior observed as a holdback/delay where batcher waits for compatibility/padding alignment rather than dispatching a small immediate batch for short sequences.
steps_to_reproduce: On a dedicated cluster with mixed workload (short queries <=32 tokens and long queries >=512 tokens), send a burst of short queries from multiple connections while 2-4 long generations are active.
Observe batch formation logs and metrics (batch.wait_ms, batch.max_seq, batch.pad_tokens).
Measure per-request first-token latency and p95/p99 over the burst window.
Verify that short requests are sometimes held for extra batch_fill_timeout windows instead of being dispatched immediately as small batches.
logs: 2026-03-11T16:15:02.112Z TRACE batcher: candidate_batch[id=8423] size=4 max_seq=640 pad_to=640 wait_ms=18
2026-03-11T16:15:02.130Z DEBUG batcher: received short_req conn=9 seq_len=12 enqueued_at=2026-03-11T16:14:59.987Z
2026-03-11T16:15:02.141Z WARN scheduler: dispatch_delay conn=9 wait_total_ms=2134 reason=pad_aligned_wait
investigation_notes: SRE replicated on staging by replaying production traffic sample; p99 tail reproduced when we mix short and long sequences concurrently.

Batcher heuristic uses max_seq_in_window to compute pad_to and holds small sequences until compatible larger sequences arrive to avoid padding inefficiency; this creates head-of-line padding waits for short sequences.
Telemetry: batch.wait_ms distribution shows a bimodal pattern. Short-req quantile (<=32 tokens) had median wait 6ms but p99 wait 1200ms during bursts.
Correlated with continuous batching config: min_batch_fill_timeout_ms=12, max_batch_size=32, adaptive_padding=true, per-tenant routing disabled.
Traces: linked trace ids: trace-prod-20260311-rc73a, trace-prod-20260311-rc7d9. See dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/dashboards/batcher-waits?range=2026-03-11T16:00/2026-03-11T17:00
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reported p99 jumps and some 504s at 16:15 UTC during a marketing spike. They observed the issue only on the dedicated cluster in us-east.

SRE (Miguel): Reproduced in staging by replaying mixed-length trace. Hypothesis: batcher is preferring to align to a large max_seq (padding) causing short requests to wait; will test lowering min_fill timeout and disabling adaptive_padding as a temporary mitigation.
Customer (BrightChat ops): Happy to try tunable changes; prefer a config we can control per-tenant while long-term root cause is fixed.

Eng (Nina Patel): Adding engineering to implement fast-path for short sequences (dispatch immediately if queue has only short sequences or connection-level hint provided). Punted to sprint 86. Related PR will include metrics to verify fix.

SRE (Miguel): Applied tenant-level override: min_batch_fill_timeout_ms=8 and adaptive_padding=false for BrightChat at 16:55 UTC. Short-sequence p99 dropped back towards baseline within 5 minutes; no further 504s observed. Awaiting customer confirmation of UX improvement.
resolution: Workaround applied: tenant override to reduce min_batch_fill_timeout_ms and disable adaptive_padding for BrightChat. Customer observed reduced p99 and no further timeouts. Engineering will implement a short-request fast-path and an opt-in per-tenant batching profile to prevent padding-driven holdbacks. Follow-up task (INT-4782) created for scheduling code change and canary rollout.
